newsitem.title: USA: Dow edges lower, temp staffing shares hit.
newsitem.headline: Dow edges lower, temp staffing shares hit.

text.p: Stocks pulled back from record heights on modest profit-taking on Thursday, with shares of companies that provide temporary workers hammered after an earnings warning from Olsten Corp.

"After the feeding frenzy of the past couple of weeks, investors are taking a bit of a breather here. There's a bit of profit-taking, nothing dramatic," said Charlie Crane, director of research at Spears Benzak Salomon & Farrell.

After setting November's 10th record high on Wednesday, the Dow Jones industrial average slipped 11.55 points to 6,418.47. In the broader market, advancing issues edged declines, 1,198 to 1,195, on heavy volume of about 468.7 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

The Nasdaq composite index lost 6.86 points to 1,258.08 as heavyweights Intel Corp. and Microsoft Corp. gave up some of their recent strong gains. Intel lost two to 118-7/8 and Microsoft was off 2-7/8 to 150-3/8.

"It looks like we're making a bit of a pitstop. Some profit-taking has kicked in but by and large the tilt appears to be up. There appears to be some nervousness about the market's big move over the past 10 days," said Alan Ackerman, a market strategist at Fahnestock and Co.
One focus for investors was temporary staffing companies. "That's all related to Olsten," said Hildegard Zagorski, a Prudential Securities market analyst.

Olsten, the most-active NYSE issue, tumbled 5-1/2 points to 14-3/8 after forecasting fourth-quarter earnings will fall well below expectations. It cited ongoing competitive pressures at its two main businesses and lower revenues from Medicare operations.
Among others in the group, Accustaff lost 2-3/8 to 21-1/8, Interim Services lost 3-1/8 to 36, Robert Half lost 2-3/8 to 35-7/8, Norrell fell 1-3/8 to 22-7/8 and Manpower fell 3/4 to 31-1/8.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury fell 4/32, or $1.25 on a $1,000 bond, raising the yield to 6.42 percent from 6.41 percent at Wednesday's close.

After the closing bell, Applied Materials reported sharply lower fourth-quarter earnings. The leading maker of water fabrication systems for the semiconductor industry also said the industry downturn could extend through early 1997.
"This might pressure the chip stocks tomorrow, specifically the commodity chip makers," said Phil Orlando of Value Line Asset Management.
Applied Materials ended up 1-1/2 to 32. In after-hours trading, it fell 1-1/8.
Among other issues, Texaco lost one to 98-7/8. The city of Philadelphia's pension board voted to divest $5.5 million worth of Texaco stock, citing evidence of racial bias at the company.

Conrail lost 2-1/4 to 94-5/8. CSX Corp. said its $110 cash tender offer for shares of Conrail was oversubscribed. CSX proceeded with its offer after a federal appeals court on Wednesday denied Norfolk Southern's effort to block it. CSX lost one to 45-5/8 and Norfolk Southern fell 1/2 to 87-1/2.
Panavision, a designer and maker of high-precision film camera systems, climbed three to 20 in its Wall Street debut.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks fell 1.20 to 742.75. The American Stock Exchange index rose 0.57 to 587.76.
The NYSE composite index of all listed common stocks edged down 0.55 to 392.25. The average share fell 6 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at 7,156.655, off 18.196 or 0.25 percent.
